PC: Assess and manage the patient’s airway by verifying patency, evaluating the presence and effort of breathing, and initiating appropriate oxygen supplementation as needed (via nasal cannula, facemask, non-rebreather mask)
Connect patient to cardiopulmonary monitor (if not on monitor already) and correctly identify the presence of sinus tachycardia, tachypnea, and persistent hypoxia
Establish IV access; however, if establishing IV access or drawing additional labs further agitates this patient, these endeavors must be abandoned in an effort to calm the child

Employ early measures to reduce pulmonary vascular resistance (i.e, put the child in mother’s arms to calm him, abandon additional needle-sticks or other noxious stimuli) and increase systemic vascular resistance (i.e., bring child’s knees to chest, or allow child to assume a position of comfort)
Consider additional pharmacologic therapies such as morphine 0.1 mg/kg for perceived pain or propranolol 0.1 mg/kg to relax right ventricular outflow tract (infundibular spasm)

If these measures are not effective, administer phenylephrine 5-20 mcg/kg bolus dose (followed by continuous infusion) to increase systemic afterload and promote flow through the right ventricular outflow tract into the pulmonary circulation

Other actions that may be taken throughout this case are:
Initiating fluid resuscitation for hypotension
Weigh pros and cons of drawing labs (e.g., ABG, CBC, BMP)
Administering bicarbonate if there is documented metabolic (lactic) acidosis as acidemia is associated with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance
MK: Verbalize a differential diagnosis for hypoxia including hyper-cyanotic spell in the setting of known Tetralogy of Fallot
SBP: Involve Cardiology and/or Cardiothoracic Surgery in the care of the patient who will need timely corrective cardiac surgery (BT, modified BT, or aortopulmonary shunt)
